lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.criterion: Communication quality, time respect, and dignified closure
findings.observation: Direct evidence: Today and Ask name an overdue, recruiter-owned internal action, its blocker, due time, and completion condition, while every action surface says that no message or external write occurs. The frozen artifact contains no candidate-facing acknowledgement, channel preference, progress update, easy reply path, rejection, or closure interaction, so candidate-side communication quality and timeliness are not directly observed.
findings.evidence: Direct: evidence/screenshots/canonical-today.png; evidence/screenshots/ask-backend-response.png; evidence/screenshots/canonical-action-outcome.png; evidence/p0-journey-runtime.json (P0-07); apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift (owner, due, outcome, and no-external-effect copy). Supported inference: this internal accountability should reduce forgotten follow-through, but it does not prove that a candidate receives a timely, candid update.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can see what they owe and recover interrupted work without accidentally contacting someone twice. A candidate could still experience silence or poorly timed communication if the human handoff is not completed, because this V1 intentionally stops before recipient delivery.
findings.recommendation: Before making a candidate-experience release claim, add a human field gate rather than an auto-send feature: define the smallest recruiter communication commitment for waiting, delay, and closure; test specific candidate-facing wording and response paths with authorized participants; and expose hiring-manager or client delay without nudging the candidate again.
findings.verification: Run an authorized recruiter comparison and candidate-side study across waiting, delay, correction, and closure. Verify time to a truthful human update, candidate effort to respond or correct, recruiter follow-through completion, and zero automatic sends; retain examples of the exact messages and observed outcomes as field evidence.

findings.criterion: Agency, informed consent, correction, and deletion scope
findings.observation: Direct evidence: audio capture requires purpose, authorizing party, authorization basis, recruiter attestation, foreground microphone success, a local-only receipt, and a revoke-and-delete control. Typed Signal deletion waits for server confirmation before removing the local payload; backend evidence redacts source-derived Proposal content, removes deletion canaries, and marks surviving authority unavailable while preserving the recruiter-confirmed value and audit receipt. The current V1 offers no candidate-operated notice, inspection, correction, revocation, or deletion-request path, and its real regional and production retention behavior is untested.
findings.evidence: Direct: evidence/screenshots/audio-authorization-receipt.png; evidence/screenshots/typed-signal-deletion.png; evidence/pursuit-evidence/pursuit-evidence-integrity-runtime.json; apps/ios/Sources/Features/AudioSignalCaptureView.swift; apps/ios/Sources/Features/AudioSignalCaptureStore.swift; apps/ios/Sources/Features/TextSignalCaptureView.swift. Supported inference: recruiter attestation and explicit authority degradation are strong local guardrails, but they are not independent proof that a real candidate understood the purpose or could exercise data rights.
findings.user_impact: The local product is unlikely to start a hidden recording or falsely erase a source after a failed server delete. In production, a mistaken or stale recruiter attestation could still leave a candidate without a clear remedy, and a broad reading of “Signal deleted” could differ from the intentional retention of a decision receipt and confirmed canonical value.
findings.recommendation: Before production use, define a candidate-comprehensible recording notice and correction, revocation, access, and deletion protocol. Make deletion confirmation state plainly what was removed, what minimal audit or recruiter-confirmed state remains, why it remains, and how it can be challenged; keep these controls human-owned and region-aware.
findings.verification: On physical devices and a production-like multi-tenant environment, execute authorized consent, revocation, correction, export/access, source deletion, derivative redaction, account deletion, retry, and recovery journeys. Use seeded canaries across operational stores and have authorized candidate participants explain the consent and deletion consequences back in their own words.

strengths: Direct: identity is never preselected; same-name records carry distinct Person, role, context, and identity clues; unresolved evidence can remain unbound instead of being guessed. The frozen iOS suite and evidence-integrity runtime pass these exact boundaries.

Direct: generated output stays internal and reviewable. Proposals cannot send messages or write external systems, owned actions report empty external effects, and 30 deterministic Agent trials produced zero external effects with only review-only Proposal or no_action authority.

Direct: response-loss and interruption states are candid and recoverable. Proposal and owned-action writes lock unknown outcomes, reconcile by the same operation reference, and do not create a second write; evidence-review authority binds the exact predecessor, superseded operations become terminal, and a nonempty Ask draft is preserved.

Direct: Ask opens the exact existing Pursuit action without recording a change, surfaces owner, due state, blocker, and completion condition, and hides stale citations until a fresh Ask. This protects human attention without pretending that technology completed the relationship work.

Direct: source deletion redacts Proposal narrative and canaries, supersedes unsafe review authority, and changes temporal copy to “Originally evidence-supported · Evidence unavailable” instead of leaving a false evidence-backed claim.
missing_evidence: A complete manual VoiceOver traversal by a human, including the consent, identity, review, recovery, deletion, and exact-action handoff paths.
Physical-device Action Button, microphone, interruption, foreground/background, and system-capture privacy behavior.
Five credentialed, pinned-model live Claude Agent SDK trials against the frozen evaluator.
Production authentication, regional consent and retention controls, real deletion and data-subject-request operations, provider reconciliation, and cross-tenant adversarial testing.

Authorized recruiter field comparison and candidate-side research covering message specificity, preferred channel and timing, waiting, correction, rejection or closure, trust, and whether any automation feels hidden or pressuring.
Observed candidate outcomes; the artifact is synthetic-only and contains no evidence that a candidate received, understood, trusted, or benefited from a follow-up.
open_questions: What minimum human communication commitment should become visible when an owned action is overdue, and how will client or hiring-manager delay be exposed without pushing the candidate again?

How will a real candidate learn that audio is being recorded, see the purpose and retention boundary, correct a mistaken authorization record, or revoke permission without depending solely on the recruiter?
When a Signal is deleted but a recruiter-confirmed value and audit receipt remain, what exact deletion copy and challenge path will make that distinction understandable and fair?
